scope: Proposition 6.4 (Information after finite splitting) of the manuscript “Localization costs and information growth for exact Gaussian observations” (preprints/Localization-costs-and-information-growth-for-exact-Gaussian-observations-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 140 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 4f43e1443f9fd513), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 35. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let z ∼ τ, and let B ≥ 0 and W ≥ 1 be integers with log W ≤ n2. Independently of z, draw independent standard Gaussian k × d matrices X1, . . . , XB, with k as fixed above. Consider a computation with a fixed initial state u0 and at most W states at each block boundary. At block b, the outgoing state ub is an everywhere-defined Borel function of (ub−1, Xb, Xbs(z)). Before each block one can reveal a finite partition label ib, determined by z and the preceding analysis history, such that the complete history H = (i1, u1, . . . , iB, uB) has finite range and satisfies I(z; H) ≤ 4C′nB for an absolute constant C′ > 0 and all sufficiently large n. The labels indicate nested dyadic cells containing z; they do not alter the computation’s state rules.
